correctness.rationale: For a colour fibre S of cardinality a in K_n minus a matching, each same-colour degree is a-1 or a-2. Thus every fibre with a<=d+1 is allowed, none with a>=d+3 is allowed, and one with a=d+2 is allowed precisely when it is a disjoint union of (d+2)/2 entire deleted edges; this forces even d. The exceptional colours and missing-edge assignments are unique and disjoint. Their labelled count is C(k,r)t!/(s!^r(t-rs)!) and each residual colour has <=d+1 vertices, giving B_{d+1}(n-2sr,k-r). Polynomial identity follows from infinitely many integer palette sizes. The r=1 exceptional configurations have degree n-d-1 and leading coefficient C(t,(d+2)/2); every r>=2 and every repeat among residual colours reduces polynomial degree. Brute original-neighbourhood checker independently verified 608 parameter profiles for n<=8, every matching size, d<=n, and k=1..4; a second finite difference test corroborates the degree claim through n=10. Finite tests are not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The motivating 2026 research asks how much structural information the defective family contains. In a dense natural two-parameter family, the theorem shows infinite uniform odd-defect blindness and an exact even-defect detection threshold. The first new coefficient is a concrete binomial count of missing-edge subsets, and the full named-colour formula counts every valid assignment for every defect, not merely extremal palettes. The parity switch is a nontrivial structural description of all monochromatic classes and not a textbook restatement of chromatic number or universal contraction.
